svg.text: PID control loop – HMC spindle coolant temperature (chiller valve), tuned two ways
Process from a step test (example): valve +20 % → coolant −4 K. Model: K = −0.2 K/%, time constant τ = 180 s, dead time θ = 30 s. PID in cyclic OB, T = 1 s.
anti-windup: stop the I-part while the output is at a limit
Tuning values (|K| = 0.2 K/%, τ = 180 s, θ = 30 s)
Ku = 50.4 %/K, Pu = 112.9 s (calculated from the model)
ZN PID: 11.8 % overshoot, settles (2 %) in 197 s, valve hits 100 %
lambda PI: 0 % overshoot, settles in 358 s, valve max 68 %
Anti-windup test (ZN PI, SP step −8 K):
without: 1.9 K overshoot, settles in 1114 s
with clamping: 0 K overshoot, settles in 405 s
Rule: start with lambda (robust), make faster only
if the process allows – check with a real step test.
block diagram, FOPDT model, ZN vs lambda tuning, step response
